strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy PR #23253 (gh-23171): RegularGridInterpolator with method='linear' on a 2D single-point grid (every axis length 1) returns NaN for float64 values at the grid point, while float32 returns the stored value. Build scipy at buggy commit 6f1dac31620c, run the developer's test test_length_one_axis_all, expect the linear-2-float64 case to fail on the buggy build, then rebuild at the fixed (PR #23253) revision and expect it to pass.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler (gcc or clang; the report used gcc 15.1.0 and clang 17.0.0)
BLAS/LAPACK backend (OpenBLAS on Linux; the report used Accelerate on darwin/aarch64)
pinned_because: python_version 3.13 is observed in the supplied environment, not a documented constraint; it is the version the reproduction runs under
numpy>=2.1 is an era-inferred choice (no documented constraint in the passages) made so numpy has Python 3.13 wheels; the strategy chooses it and says so

pybind11, Cython and pythran versions (2.13.6, 3.1.2, 0.18.0) are observed in the issue #23171 build report, not constraints; prefer whatever pyproject.toml pins at the buggy commit, falling back to those observed values

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/interpolate/tests/test_rgi.py::TestInterpN::test_length_one_axis_all (parametrized over dtype in float32/float64, ndim in 1/2/3, method in linear/nearest); the failing case is the linear-2-float64 parametrization
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 6f1dac31620c, the test_length_one_axis_all[linear-2-float64] case fails at the first xp_assert_equal on the valid sample, because the interpolator returns NaN where 1/7 is expected; the other parametrizations pass. On the fixed revision (PR #23253), all parametrizations of test_length_one_axis_all pass, including linear-2-float64, which returns the stored value 1/7 at the grid point and the fill value 1/42 out of bounds.
strategy.numerical_probe: rgi = RegularGridInterpolator(points=(np.array([0.]), np.array([0.])), values=np.array([[1/7]]), method='linear'); rgi([[0., 0.]]) should give array([0.14285714]) on the fixed build and array([nan]) on the buggy build
risks: Test-name mismatch: the developer's diff defines test_length_one_axis_all, but the commit message names the failing case test_length_one_axes[linear-2-float64]. Use the diff's name for the command and check the parametrization id actually reported by pytest.

Backend dependence: the report came from darwin/aarch64 with Accelerate. The bug is in the Cython evaluate_linear_2d branch, not in BLAS, so it should reproduce on Linux with OpenBLAS, but this is inferred, not shown. If it does not reproduce on Linux, retry on the reporting platform (macOS arm64 with Accelerate) before concluding the transition cannot happen.

Compiler dependence: the Cython code is compiled by the C compiler, so optimisation level or compiler could in principle change NaN handling. This is unverified; if the failure does not show, try the reporting compiler (clang 17).

numpy version is unbounded in the evidence and numerically relevant. An unpinned numpy may not match the one the buggy revision was tested with, which could change dtype promotion in the test (linear promotes to float64).

Buggy and fixed builds must both be rebuilt; the editable install compiles Cython at import, so stale .so files from the other revision would give a false transition. Clean the build directory between checkouts.
Expected values beyond the reproducer are incomplete in the passages; the test's 1/7 and 1/42 values are taken from the diff, not independently confirmed.

Removing the NaN branches means NaN or out-of-bounds inputs now depend on bounds_error and fill handling; the test's NaN-input assertions may be affected by unrelated changes in the same PR, so a failure there that is not on linear-2-float64 should be investigated separately.

oracle.reference_source: the stored grid value itself (1/7 cast to the test dtype) and fill_value 1/42, as set in the developer's test
oracle.why: With a single grid point no interpolation is possible, so the expected output is the stored value exactly; the test compares with xp_assert_equal, which is exact.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the valid-sample check interp_fill(sample) for linear-2-float64 returns array([nan]); xp_assert_equal against array([1/7]) fails because NaN is not equal to 1/7, which is the transition.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the linear-2-float64 case returns the stored value at the grid point and the fill value out of bounds, so every xp_assert_equal and pytest.raises check passes.
